summary: Botswana is one of Africa’s easiest destinations to enter — citizens of some 100 countries, including the EU, US, UK, most of the Commonwealth and most SADC states, get up to 90 visa-free days, while the remaining nationalities apply through the official eVisa portal or a Botswana mission before traveling.

safety.text: Attacks on tourists are rare, but violent crime is increasing, particularly in Gaborone, Francistown and Maun, and there have been isolated thefts from lodges in the Chobe area. Outside the towns, stray wildlife and livestock make driving dangerous, especially after dark; carry water and fuel on trips to remote areas.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says travellers under 18 must show border officials a certified copy of their original birth certificate and a valid passport, plus a written consent form from any parent not travelling with them if they travel alone or with only one parent. The UK FCDO says the birth certificate is needed on entry and exit.
The UK FCDO warns that driving outside the major urban areas can be dangerous because of stray wildlife and livestock, particularly at night, so take extra care after dark.

Australia's Smartraveller says malaria occurs throughout Botswana and is widespread in the north, especially in the rainy season from November to March, and suggests considering malaria prevention if you travel north of Gaborone. Use insect repellent.
Visa-free visitors may spend at most 90 days in Botswana within any 12-month period — extensions beyond your stamped stay are requested at an immigration office before it expires.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Botswana?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not — citizens of around 100 countries, including the US, UK, EU members, most Commonwealth states and most SADC states, enter visa-free for up to 90 days. Nationalities that do need a visa (including India, China and most of the former Soviet states) apply in advance through the official eVisa portal (evisa.gov.bw) or a Botswana mission; there is no visa on arrival.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Botswana visa-free?
faq.answer: You are normally stamped in for up to 90 days, capped at 90 days in total within any 12-month period. Extensions within the cap can be requested at immigration offices in Gaborone and other towns before your stay expires.

faq.question: Do Indian and Chinese citizens need a visa for Botswana?
faq.answer: Yes — both currently need a visa obtained in advance, most conveniently through the official eVisa portal. Botswana has periodically reviewed its policy toward these markets, so check for updates shortly before booking.

faq.question: What documents do children need to enter Botswana?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says all travellers under 18 must present a certified copy of their original birth certificate and a valid passport. Minors travelling alone or with only one parent also need a written consent form from the parent or parents not travelling.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for Botswana?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from or transit through a yellow fever risk country. Coming directly from Europe, North America or South Africa, no certificate is needed.
